title: Knocking down of p53 triggers apoptosis and autophagy, concomitantly with inhibition of migration on SSC-4 oral squamous carcinoma cells.

baseline_assertions: Knocking down of p53 triggers apoptosis and autophagy, concomitantly with inhibition of migration on SSC-4 oral squamous carcinoma cells.
In SSC-4 cells, inhibiting the expression of p53 decreased the proliferation ability, induced apoptosis/autophagy, and decreased migration.
findings.rationale: One knockdown phenotype experiment retains apoptosis/autophagy, reduced proliferation and reduced migration.
source_evidence: Knocking down of p53 triggers apoptosis and autophagy, concomitantly with inhibition of migration on SSC-4 oral squamous carcinoma cells.

We observed that inhibiting the expression of p53 decreased the proliferation ability and induced apoptosis/autophagy in SSC-4 cells. Moreover, we observed that this has decreased migration and has blocked the expression of VEGF.
